## How this page works

One probe is one idea from the [O2 papers](../00-research/o2-self-relevant-action.qmd),
tested once, in a single sitting, with the smallest model and sample that could
possibly show the effect. Every probe gets a written verdict even when the
result is boring. Anything interesting gets promoted to a full experiment with
its own page, the way the [SelfAware replication](selfaware.qmd) did.

Rules to keep this cheap:

1. One idea per probe, one run, no sweeps.
2. Smallest model and sample that could show the effect.
3. Record the verdict the same day: **promote**, **dead end**, or **unclear**.
4. A dead end stays on the page. It saves re-testing the idea later.

## Probe queue

Ideas waiting, pulled from the paper notes:

- **Run SAD-LITE on one newer model.** Laine [9] flagged it as runnable: 13 tasks,
  no per-model setup, no logprobs needed. Does the knowing/acting gap look the
  same on a 2026 model?
- **Add a third action to the abstain test.** Wang [6] only offers answer or
  abstain. Reuse the frozen SelfAware sample and offer answer / abstain /
  ask for more information, and see whether the extra option changes the tradeoff.
- **Run an awareness judge over my own prompts.** Li [14] lists eight factors
  that make a setup read as a test; my materials likely trip F1, F4 and F7.
  Cheapest version: ask a model whether my prompts look like an evaluation.
- **Byte-identical controls.** Nayan [15] used 120 identical prompt pairs to
  measure harness noise before trusting any behavioural delta. Worth copying
  before any probe here gets believed.
